articles.title: Track the training you actually did
articles.summary: A training log is a description, not a verdict. Record what you did, how it felt, and any practical barrier you encountered. The purpose is to make the next decision better informed.
body: A training log is a description, not a verdict. Record what you did, how it felt, and any practical barrier you encountered. The purpose is to make the next decision better informed.

Avoid interpreting one unusually good or bad session as a trend. Look for patterns over time and keep the plan appropriate to your current ability. General public-health guidance does not replace individualized advice, especially when pain, illness, or a medical condition changes what is suitable.
